articles.title: China’s Air Force One: Inside Xi Jinping’s Boeing 747-8 Presidential Jet
articles.summary: International News: While much of the world is familiar with America's Air Force One, China's presidential transport arrangements remain far less known, even though they .
articles.body: While much of the world is familiar with America's Air Force One, China's presidential transport arrangements remain far less known, even though they are based on the same variant of the iconic Boeing-747. Air travel for China's top leadership—the CCP General Secretary, President, Premier and other senior officials —is managed by the 34th Division of the People's Liberation Army Air Force, which operates a fleet including six Boeing 737-300s, two 737-700s, four 737-800s, three Airbus A319s and ten Bombardier Challenger 800s. Notably, Chinese regulations restrict the use of dedicated presidential aircraft strictly to the President and the State Council Premier for international visits, other state leaders are required to use chartered planes instead.For Xi Jinping's own long-haul international travel, the aircraft of choice has been a specially converted Boeing 747-8I, carrying Air China branding and registration B-2479, converted and tested around 2016-2017 for exclusive head-of-state use. While no official photographs have ever been released, the aircraft is widely believed to be fitted with conference tables, private bedrooms and office suites—features expected of any long-range VIP transport. In the past, China has also used converted commercial Air China Boeing 747-400 aircraft for international travel when required, with three such aircraft carrying the registrations B-2445, B-2447 and B-2472.The Boeing 747-8, the aircraft at the heart of this fleet, is the final and largest member of the 747 family ever built, stretched to 250 feet in length, making it the longest airliner in commercial service. It features a deeper, thicker wing for greater fuel capacity, larger raked wingtips for improved aerodynamics, and more efficient GENx engines borrowed from the 787 Dreamliner, pushing its maximum takeoff weight to nearly 975,000 pounds, the heaviest of any Boeing airliner.China isn't the only nation to have turned to this aircraft for head-of-state duties. VIP-configured 747-8Is have also gone to Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Brunei, Morocco, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, the last of which is used by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Interestingly, the United States itself has recently adopted a version of the same aircraft, designated the VC-25B Bridge, a stopgap presidential transport built from a former Qatari VIP jet gifted to Washington in 2025, now used by President Trump while the definitive VC-25A replacements remain under development.India, Japan, Israel, Indonesia, Singapore, Bangladesh, South Africa and a few other nations use variants of the more modern Boeing-777. The Indian Air Force acquired the Boeing-777 from Air India when the government divested from the firm. The IAF also acquired six A-321 aircraft from Air India, these aircraft will be converted to Airborne Early Warning and Control aircraft.

articles.title: San Francisco minted just 24 of these dimes in 1894 and only 9 are known to survive; 132 years later, one 10-cent coin has sold at auction for $1.25 million
articles.summary: US News: A 10-cent coin minted in San Francisco more than a century ago has just sold for about $1.25 million, turning one of the smallest denominations in US .
articles.body: A 10-cent coin minted in San Francisco more than a century ago has just sold for about $1.25 million, turning one of the smallest denominations in US currency into a million-dollar collector's prize. The 1894-S Barber dime is one of the most famous rarities in American numismatics. According to auction house Stack's Bowers Galleries, which handled the recent sale, only 24 examples were struck in 1894 and just nine are known to survive today. The coin sold for $1,250,500 at the company's 2026 auction, more than 130 years after it was made.Why were only 24 dimes made?The extraordinary story of the 1894-S Barber dime begins at the San Francisco Mint during a period of economic difficulty. The United States was still dealing with the effects of the Panic of 1893, a severe financial crisis that contributed to a sharp reduction in demand for new coinage. Against that backdrop, just 24 Barber dimes were struck at the San Francisco Mint in June 1894. They were not ordinary coins produced in large quantities for everyday circulation. The tiny mintage eventually turned the dime into one of the great rarities of American coin collecting. The exact reason for the unusual production has never been established with complete certainty. According to evidence from the San Francisco Mint, a small quantity of subsidiary coin bullion remained after recoinage and was enough to produce 24 dimes. Another long-standing story says Mint Superintendent John Daggett had the coins struck for prominent banker friends and gave some to his daughter.The competing explanations are part of what has made the 1894-S dime so fascinating to collectors. Its rarity is certain; the circumstances surrounding its creation remain partly mysterious.A tiny coin with a famous designThe coin belongs to the Barber dime series, which was designed by Charles E. Barber, then chief engraver of the US Mint. The series was produced from 1892 to 1916. The obverse features Liberty wearing a cap, while the reverse carries the denomination "ONE DIME" inside a wreath. The small "S" mint mark on the reverse identifies the coin as having been produced at the San Francisco Mint.Although collectors can find Barber dimes from other years, the 1894-S issue is in a completely different category because of its extremely small mintage and tiny surviving population. Only nine examples are currently known to exist. That means every time one of these coins comes onto the market, collectors are competing for an object that almost never becomes available.From a 10-cent coin to a $1.25 million treasureThe latest sale demonstrates just how dramatically rarity can transform the value of an old coin. The 1894-S Barber dime that recently went under the hammer sold for $1,250,500 at Stack's Bowers Galleries on September 1, 2026. The latest sale is also part of a much longer history of extraordinary prices for the coin. One of the surviving dimes has changed hands for millions of dollars in previous years, with its value driven not simply by its age but by the combination of scarcity, historical mystery and collector demand.The 1894-S dime is particularly notable because its entire known population is small enough to make each specimen significant. A coin does not need to be thousands of years old to become extraordinarily valuable; in this case, a piece of American currency from the late 19th century has acquired a status approaching that of a national numismatic treasure.The dime that helped make Dave Bowers famousThe 1894-S dime also has an important connection to Dave Bowers, the legendary American numismatist and co-founder of Stack's Bowers Galleries. According to the auction house's history of the coin, Bowers purchased an 1894-S dime in 1957, when he was just 19 years old, for $4,750. At the time, spending thousands of dollars on a 10-cent coin was an extraordinary decision for a young collector.Bowers later sold the coin for $6,000. That early transaction became an important episode in his career and helped establish his reputation in the world of rare coins. The dime therefore became connected not only with American numismatic history but also with one of the most influential figures in the modern coin-collecting business.Why this dime remains legendaryThe appeal of the 1894-S Barber dime goes beyond its face value or even its silver content. Its story combines a mysterious origin, an exceptionally small mintage, a handful of surviving examples and decades of fascination among collectors. Of the original 24 coins, only nine are known today. That scarcity means that each surviving example represents a tiny piece of a production run that was never repeated.More than 130 years after the San Francisco Mint produced those 24 dimes, one of them has once again demonstrated why the coin is considered legendary. What began as a 10-cent piece in 1894 has become an object capable of commanding around $1.25 million at auction, showing how rarity and history can turn an ordinary denomination into one of the most coveted coins in American collecting.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Global South must be rule-shaper, India ready to take lead': PM Modi at Brics Summit
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday officially declared the Brics Summit 2026 open, welcoming world leaders, including Russian Preside.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday officially declared the Brics Summit 2026 open, welcoming world leaders, including Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, to India for the two-day summit.Addressing the leaders at the opening session, PM Modi said India’s Brics chairship had followed a “people-centric and humanity-first approach”, with resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability identified as key priorities.Here are the top quotes:This year’s Brics Summit marks a historic milestone as we celebrate the 20th anniversary of Brics. In human life, the age of 20 marks the beginning of a new phase of maturity and responsibility. It is a stage when responsibilities are added to dreams and capabilities are given a new direction.India’s Brics chairship is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. Resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability have been our priorities. With these priorities, we have placed special emphasis on connecting the BRICS chairship with the common people. With this vision, more than 350 meetings were organised, and we had the opportunity to welcome your teams in nearly 30 cities.Today, Brics, too, is at its coming-of-age moment. Over the past 20 years, Brics has established a distinct identity on the global stage. We respect each other’s perspectives and move forward through consensus. We are not against anyone; rather, we seek to move forward with the approach of taking everyone along.Reform in UNSC cannot be delayed anymore.Global South must become a rule-shaper. The current structure of global governance appears like a pyramid. At the top, power and decision-making are concentrated, while at the bottom are countries that are affected by these decisions but have little role in shaping them. The Global South is today on the frontlines of global crises, but in the back row when it comes to decision-making. I propose a Brics continuity and implementation mechanism. Under this, all initiatives and outcomes can be followed up through the Troika. We can create a secure digital repository where, along with every decision, the nodal point, timeline and implementation status can be recorded. Friends, while strengthening Brics, we must also chart the course for global reform.For the next 20 years, we need to work on a new and ambitious agenda. We must begin this with our own working system. The Brics chairmanship changes every year, but this should not cause our institutional momentum to slow down.Friends, the message from this Brics Summit being hosted by India should be clear. If our future is shared, the right to shape that future should also be shared. From voice to impact, from privilege to partnership, this should be the guiding resolve of Brics at present.Meanwhile, in a major diplomatic breakthrough, Brics nations have reached a consensus on a Joint Statement following intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday. The statement is expected to be issued during the summit later today.The negotiations involved differences over several contentious issues, with India leading sustained consultations to bridge competing positions and build consensus among member countries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian-origin woman shot dead by stalker in California; mother says ‘system failed her’
articles.summary: US News: A 38-year-old Indian-origin woman was shot dead outside a restaurant in California’s Sacramento after allegedly being stalked and harassed for months .
articles.body: A 38-year-old Indian-origin woman was shot dead outside a restaurant in California’s Sacramento after allegedly being stalked and harassed for months by a 22-year-old man, who later died by suicide during a police standoff on a busy highway.Shalini Thakur was being dropped off at work at a shopping plaza in Sacramento’s Arden Arcade area on Tuesday when Rohit allegedly approached and confronted her, according to the Sacramento County Sheriff’s Office.When Thakur tried to flee, Rohit chased her and shot her multiple times outside a Panera Bread restaurant near Howe and Northrop avenues, investigators said. She was pronounced dead at the scene.Months of stalking and harassmentInvestigators said Rohit had been stalking and harassing Thakur for months. Thakur found an Apple AirTag hidden under her car in January, while the harassment allegedly escalated to Rohit deflating her vehicle’s tyre and following her to work.He also allegedly obtained a copy of her apartment key and entered her home while she was sleeping. When confronted, Rohit reportedly claimed he had entered because he was concerned something had happened to her after she failed to answer him.Thakur initially declined to pursue criminal charges or seek a restraining order, but deputies remained in contact with her. In May, sheriff’s officials again urged her to obtain one, which she eventually did.On July 29, Rohit allegedly violated the restraining order by leaving random grocery items at her front door. Deputies attempted to contact him twice after the incident, according to the sheriff’s office.Suspect tracked to Highway 50After the shooting, witnesses provided investigators with information about Rohit’s vehicle. Deputies entered the details into the Sacramento County Sheriff’s Office’s FLOCK automated license plate reader system and located the vehicle within minutes on eastbound Highway 50 near Watt Avenue.When deputies attempted to pull Rohit over, he stopped on the freeway, leading to a police standoff that brought traffic to a standstill for hours.Rohit was later found slumped over in the driver’s seat with what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities confirmed he had died from the wound. KCRA 3 reported that deputies did not appear to have fired their weapons.‘Police did not protect my daughter’In an emotional interview with KCRA 3, Thakur’s mother said authorities failed to protect her daughter despite the months-long stalking and harassment.“Police did not protect my daughter,” she said.Investigators said Rohit had no known local criminal history. Authorities are continuing to investigate the killing, the stalking allegations and the circumstances surrounding Rohit’s death.DHS confirms suspect was in US illegallyThe Department of Homeland Security said Friday that Rohit was from India and entered the US through Arizona in 2023. A DHS spokesperson said he had previously been arrested by US Border Patrol and released by the Biden administration.“This illegal alien from India harassed, stalked, and then killed a 38-year-old woman in California, and then took his own life when police caught up to him,” a DHS spokesperson said.The spokesperson blamed the Biden administration for releasing Rohit and said the killing could have been prevented. However, the exact details of his immigration status were not immediately clear, while federal court records showed his case was pending.A Sacramento County Sheriff’s Office spokesman told KCRA 3 that the local agency does not have access to immigration-status information.California’s sanctuary law, SB 54, limits local law enforcement’s ability to cooperate with federal immigration authorities in certain circumstances. A spokesperson for Governor Gavin Newsom’s office rejected attempts to link the killing to the state’s sanctuary policies, saying the case instead raised questions about preventing stalking and domestic violence and keeping victims safe.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: A 22-year-old man and his alleged girlfriend have been arrested in connection with the murder of his wife in Delhi's Prahladpur last month.Police said their relationship emerged as the motive behind the killing.The accused, identified as Md Lal Babu alias Zahid Ali and Rukhsar Khatoon, were arrested following an extensive investigation that involved scrutiny of more than 300 CCTV cameras across Delhi, Ghaziabad, Noida, Patna, Sitamarhi, Muzaffarpur and Mumbai, police said on Saturday.According to police, Lal Babu allegedly conspired with Rukhsar and murdered his wife Sabilla Khatun inside the bathroom of a house in Prahladpur.A case under Section 103(1) (murder) of the BNS was registered at the Shahbad Dairy police station on August 29 following the murder, they said.Police said Lal Babu and Sabilla were married and lived in Prahladpur, adding that the former was allegedly in a relationship with Rukhsar and wanted to marry her.After the murder, Lal Babu allegedly fled Delhi with his minor son towards Noida, where he contacted his maternal cousin Md Osama, police said.Osama allegedly provided shelter and assistance to Lal Babu and facilitated his movement towards Bihar to evade arrest. He was arrested earlier in the investigation and sent to judicial custody, police said.Following the murder, police conducted searches at multiple locations and carried out technical analysis and field verification to track the accused.Investigators traced the routes and locations allegedly used by Lal Babu after the crime and eventually located him and Rukhsar, police said.Police said the investigation involved analysis of CCTV footage and technical inputs, along with local intelligence developed across several states.Lal Babu, a resident of Sitamarhi in Bihar, is the main accused and the husband of the deceased, police said. articles.title: ‘New & ambitious agenda’: PM Modi proposes Brics continuity mechanism with Troika system, digital repository
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday proposed a new implementation and continuity mechanism for Brics, anchored by a “Troika” system an.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday proposed a new implementation and continuity mechanism for Brics, anchored by a “Troika” system and a secure digital repository to track decisions, nodal points and timelines as the grouping’s annual presidencies rotate.Addressing the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi under India’s 2026 chairship, PM Modi said a seamless follow-up mechanism was essential to maintain institutional momentum as Brics entered its third decade and began shaping an ambitious agenda for the next 20 years.“We need to work on a new and ambitious agenda for the next 20 years. We must begin this process with our own internal working systems. While the Brics presidency rotates annually, this should not disrupt our institutional momentum. I propose the establishment of a Brics continuity and implementation mechanism,” PM Modi said.He said the proposed mechanism would allow initiatives and outcomes to be followed up through the Troika arrangement.“This would enable the follow-up of all initiatives and outcomes through the 'Troika' arrangement. We could also create a secure digital repository to record the nodal point, timeframe, and implementation status associated with every decision,” PM Modi said.The Troika mechanism provides for coordination among the previous, current and incoming Brics chairs to ensure continuity as the presidency changes annually.The proposed system draws a parallel with the G20 Troika, under which the previous, current and incoming presidencies work together to maintain continuity in the grouping’s agenda and priorities. PM Modi’s proposal seeks to apply a similar continuity framework to Brics, alongside a digital repository to track the implementation of decisions.PM Modi calls for time-bound global governance reformsAlongside reforms to Brics' internal working system, PM Modi called for time-bound changes to global multilateral institutions, saying reform of the United Nations Security Council could no longer be delayed.He proposed a three-pillar framework of Representation, Responsiveness and Rule-making to guide the future roadmap for global governance and the Global South.“In formulating this roadmap, we must focus on three key aspects: Representation, Responsiveness, and Rule-making. Regarding representation, I would like to state that reform of the UN Security Council can no longer be postponed. Negotiations on this matter must be linked to a definite timeframe and clear outcomes,” PM Modi said.He also called for voting power, leadership positions and policy priorities within international financial institutions to reflect current economic realities.“Countries that drive global economic growth should also play an appropriate role in shaping global economic governance,” he said.PM Modi said developing countries continued to face an imbalance in global decision-making and proposed that Brics members jointly formulate 10 proposals for global governance reform, with the aim of finalising them as a Brics reform roadmap by the next summit.“Today, the Global South stands in the front row of global crises but in the back row of decision-making. We must transform this 'pyramid of privilege' into a 'platform of partnership'—one where every nation has a voice, every member has a stake, and the development of humanity lies at the heart of every endeavour,” he said.The Prime Minister said the existing global governance structure resembled a pyramid, with power and decision-making concentrated at the top while countries affected by those decisions remained unable to shape them.“While strengthening Brics, we must also chart a course for global reform. The current structure of global governance resembles a pyramid: power and decision-making are concentrated at the top, while the lower tiers consist of nations that are affected by these decisions yet unable to shape them,” PM Modi said.The Prime Minister said the Global South must become a “rule shaper” to deal with the challenges facing the world. He also proposed a seafarers’ network among Brics countries to ensure their safety.Brics marks 20 years as India hosts summitPM Modi thanked participating countries for their contribution and support during India’s Brics chairship, describing the grouping’s 20th anniversary as a historic milestone.“I express my heartfelt gratitude to all of you for your active contribution and support in making India’s Brics chairmanship a success. This year’s Brics summit marks a historic milestone. We are celebrating the 20th anniversary of Brics. In human life, the age of 20 marks the beginning of a new phase of maturity and responsibility,” he said.India is hosting the 18th Brics Summit under its 2026 chairship, with the grouping entering its third decade.The summit is expected to deliberate on protecting developing economies from the global impact of wars in Ukraine and West Asia.PM Modi also said Brics had established a distinct identity on the global stage and was “not against anyone”.The summit is being attended by leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.Other leaders attending include Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung.Joint statement after intensive negotiationsA joint statement is also set to be issued by Brics nations during the summit after intensive negotiations.The negotiations continued until 4 am on Saturday, with differences reported on several contentious issues. India led consultations to bridge competing positions and build consensus among members.The statement comes against the backdrop of differing positions among Brics members, including Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE, on regional and geopolitical issues.India assumed the Brics chairship for 2026 under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”The theme focuses on strengthening existing achievements and institutional effectiveness while placing development, sustainability and innovation at the centre of the grouping’s agenda.PM Modi welcomed Brics delegates, including Xi and Putin, to Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi.Brics has emerged as a platform for cooperation among major emerging economies, with its agenda covering development, finance, technology, trade and people-to-people exchanges.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Brazil’s 200 million termite mounds are up to 4,000 years old, but they are made from soil termites dug out while building tunnels
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Across northeastern Brazil, an extraordinary landscape hides a secret beneath its surface. Around 200 million earthen mounds stretch across roughly 23.
articles.body: Across northeastern Brazil, an extraordinary landscape hides a secret beneath its surface. Around 200 million earthen mounds stretch across roughly 230,000 square kilometres, an area about the size of Great Britain. Some of these structures are almost 4,000 years old, yet they are not termite nests in the usual sense. Instead, they are enormous piles of soil excavated as Syntermes dirus termites carved out a vast network of interconnected underground tunnels. Over generations, the insects repeatedly carried earth to the surface, creating millions of evenly spaced cones. What looks like a field of ancient nests is actually the product of a hidden subterranean system.200 million termite mounds contain over 10 cubic kilometres of soilAccording to the study published in Cell Biology, titled ‘A vast 4,000-year-old spatial pattern of termite mounds’, the age of the landscape is another part of the mystery. Researchers collected soil from the centres of 11 mounds and used optically stimulated luminescence dating to determine when the material had been deposited. The resulting ages ranged from about 690 to 3,820 years ago, showing that some of the mounds have persisted for almost 4,000 years. The researchers noted that these ages are comparable with some of the oldest termite mounds known from Africa.The ancient dates also point to a process that continued over a very long period rather than a landscape created in a single episode. The researchers estimated that each mound contains about 50 cubic metres of soil. Across roughly 200 million mounds, that amounts to more than 10 cubic kilometres of excavated earth, which they compared with the volume of around 4,000 Great Pyramids of Giza. The study described the result as the greatest known example of ecosystem engineering by a single insect species.Brazil’s termite mounds have no chambers insideThe researchers inspected hundreds of structures exposed by road construction and carried out their own excavations. Rather than finding the chambers, passages and other elaborate features normally associated with termite nests, they found that each mound was essentially an amorphous mass of soil without an internal structure.Newly forming mounds contained a large central tunnel underground and connected to an extensive network of passages and narrow horizontal galleries. Some of these galleries contained harvested pieces of dead leaves or termite brood. The researchers found no royal chamber in or beneath the mounds' extensive searches, while the tunnels were sealed rather than left open to the outside, indicating that they were not simply ventilation structures.Why termites built the vast underground tunnel networkThe researchers proposed that the enormous tunnel network developed because the termites needed reliable access to food in a difficult environment. The caatinga forests of northeastern Brazil are seasonally dry, and leaf-fall occurs episodically. At night, groups of roughly 10 to 50 workers and soldiers emerge from temporary openings between the mounds to collect available food. Those small tubes are then sealed after use.According to the researchers, the permanent underground network allowed the termites to move safely through the landscape while reducing the effort needed to dispose of excavated soil. Rather than constructing each mound as a living chamber, the insects appear to have deposited the waste material generated by their underground construction. Over thousands of years, this repeated process produced the strikingly regular pattern visible across the Brazilian landscape.Brazil’s 200 million termite mounds are evenly spacedThe researchers measured the distances between neighbouring mounds and found an average separation of about 20 metres. Their analysis showed the mounds were dispersed, meaning they were more evenly distributed than would be expected from a random arrangement. With an estimated density of about 1,800 mounds per square kilometre, the researchers estimated approximately 200 million mounds.The study considered whether competition between termite colonies could explain the spacing, but experiments did not support that explanation. S. dirus workers and soldiers did not show aggression when encountered around the mounds, although termites placed in contact with individuals from 50 kilometres away became aggressive immediately. Instead, the researchers suggested that the spacing emerged through self-organisation as the insects used their interconnected tunnels to reach food and dispose of waste efficiently.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Candace Owens marked the first anniversary of Charlie Kirk’s death by dedicating a podcast episode to the late political activist. In an open letter, Owens reflected on her relationship with Kirk while making a series of unverified claims about the circumstances surrounding his death and the online circulation of footage. Her comments have renewed attention around Kirk’s legacy and the questions she says still trouble her.Candace Owens says Charlie Kirk was betrayedOwens used the anniversary to address Kirk directly, describing what she said was an immediate feeling that something had gone wrong even before she learned he had died. She said she expressed that belief to her husband, George, while they were praying in an office.“I want you to know that I already know, so you don't need to keep insisting. You know, before we even found out that you didn't make it, I knew you were betrayed. I told George that as we prayed in his office, I said, "They betrayed him."”Owens then suggested that people she believes were responsible for the alleged betrayal would eventually face consequences. She framed the situation in spiritual terms and said she believed a mistake had been made.“Instantly, Charlie, like an old memory, had just been triggered. I also know that they're not going to get away with it. They made a mistake. The devil overplayed his hand this time,” Owens added.Those statements represent Owens’ interpretation. The supplied report does not establish that Kirk was betrayed or identify evidence proving such a claim.Candace Owens questions Charlie Kirk death footageOwens also focused on the online distribution of footage showing Kirk’s fatal shooting. She questioned why the video appeared across several major social media platforms and argued that its circulation seemed unusual.“I have this deep sense that they wanted me to see you die. The manner in which it was broadcast globally all across social media doesn't make any sense. It defied algorithmic norms. Facebook, TikTok, X.”She continued by questioning why content moderation systems did not appear to remove the violent material immediately.“Suddenly, all of their preventative measures that are designed to catch and remove violence from their platforms immediately malfunctioned that day. They wanted everyone to watch you die. For what reason, I'm not sure,” Owens said.Her remarks raise questions about how graphic material spreads online, but the claims about intentional distribution remain allegations rather than established conclusions.Owens also discussed Kirk’s memorial service, saying she viewed the event as resembling a Republican National Convention rally. She brought up Ben Shapiro’s relationship with Turning Point USA and revisited her previous comments about Kirk’s reported opinion of Shapiro.Kirk died on September 10 of the previous year after being shot during an event at Utah Valley University. A suspect, Tyler Robinson, was identified in connection with the shooting.As the anniversary brought Kirk’s death back into public discussion, Owens used the occasion to voice unresolved suspicions and personal beliefs. Her comments have attracted attention, but distinguishing those allegations from confirmed facts remains important when discussing such a high-profile killing.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Brics New Delhi Declaration adopted: Terrorism, conflict resolution, tariff concerns addressed; key points
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Brics countries on Saturday unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026 at the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi. The 45-page decla.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Brics countries on Saturday unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026 at the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi. The 45-page declaration, comprising 140 points, was discussed under the theme “Strengthening Cooperation to Promote Fair Competition, including in Renewable Energy Markets”, with the aim of supporting sustainable energy transitions.“No member has raised any objection. The New Delhi Declaration 2026 is adopted unanimously,” PM Modi said at the summit.The declaration focused on condemning terrorism, conflict prevention and peaceful resolution of disputes, stronger multilateralism and concerns over unilateral trade measures.PM Modi, in his separate opening remarks, called for reforms in global governance and proposed 10 measures to be developed into a Brics reform roadmap. He also called for greater representation of the Global South in international decision-making, describing the existing system as a “pyramid of privilege” that should become a “platform of partnership”.India is chairing Brics in 2026 under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”.Brics New Delhi Declaration - full textKey points of the declarationThe Declaration addressed various key issues and concerns affecting the global order, such as:TerrorismBrics strongly condemned terrorism in all forms, including cross-border terrorism, terrorism financing and safe havens, condemned the April 22, 2025, terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, and called for zero tolerance, accountability and early adoption of the UN Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism. "We commend India for hosting the Outreach/BRICS Plus Dialogue segment of the 18thBRICS Summit, which injects new impetus to strengthen international cooperation andsolidarity," it further statedBrics cooperationThe bloc reaffirmed its commitment to mutual respect, sovereign equality, solidarity, inclusiveness and consensus, and pledged to strengthen cooperation across its three pillars: political and security, economic and financial, and cultural and people-to-people cooperation.Conflict preventionBrics countries stressed the importance of efforts to prevent conflicts, including by addressing their root causes. The declaration reaffirmed a commitment to resolving disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy. Brics further urged all parties to uphold the Gaza ceasefire and ensure unhindered humanitarian aid, opposed the forced displacement of Palestinians, and reaffirmed support for a two-state solution with an independent Palestinian state based on the internationally recognised 1967 borders.The declaration was adopted on the first day of the two-day Summit being hosted by India in New Delhi. The joint declaration came after intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday, with India leading efforts to bridge differences between the UAE and Iran over the West Asia conflict. The talks followed an earlier Brics foreign ministers’ meeting under India’s presidency that ended without a consensus, prompting prolonged negotiations to ensure the summit concluded with a joint statement.Women’s empowermentBrics recognised women as leaders, decision-makers and drivers of economic growth and social transformation, stressing their participation in governance, economic life, peacebuilding and climate action."We affirm that women's participation in governance; their financial and digital inclusion; their capacity building, access to skill development and entrepreneurship opportunities, support to entrepreneurship, access to productive and social services and their crucial role in climate action, food security and nutrition, which are interconnected is key for sustainable development," the declaration said."We also recognise the importance of policies that support women's full participation in economic life, including through appropriate care policies, in accordance with national circumstances," the leaders further said.Local currencies' pushBrics backed efforts to promote cross-border payments and trade settlements using member countries’ local currencies, while respecting national priorities. “We acknowledge the work done to study the cross-border interoperability of payment and messaging channels, and the discussions on promoting trade settlements and investments using BRICS local currencies,” the declaration stated.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), in coordination with the ministry of external affairs (MEA), ministry of home affairs (MHA) and .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), in coordination with the ministry of external affairs (MEA), ministry of home affairs (MHA) and Punjab Police, has secured the extradition of Red Notice subject Amritpal Singh alias Gurpal Singh from Moldova to India, the agency said.Singh is wanted in multiple serious criminal cases in Punjab, including double murder using firearms and offences under the Arms Act and NDPS Act. His criminal antecedents also include cases related to forgery, cheating, use of forged documents and violations of the Passport Act, according to the CBI.Arrest in Moldova after Interpol Red NoticeThe extradition followed a request from Punjab Police, after which the CBI secured an Interpol Red Notice against Singh. He was subsequently located and arrested by Moldovan authorities.Following due legal process, Moldova granted his extradition to India, the CBI said.A four-member Punjab Police team travelled to Chisinau, Moldova, to bring Singh back to India. The team, along with Singh, arrived in Delhi on September 12.Wanted in multiple Punjab casesSingh, also known as Amrit Dalam, was among the most wanted gangsters linked to the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria gang. The report said he was detained near the Moldova border based on an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of Punjab Police in coordination with the MEA, CBI and other central agencies.He’s a native of Dalam Nangal village in Batala and had fled India using a fake passport and was allegedly making extortion calls to businessmen, particularly in the Amritsar region.Punjab Police had also established the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC), headed by IG-Counterintelligence Ashish Choudhary, to track criminals hiding abroad and pursue their extradition to Punjab.Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav had said Singh was wanted in several serious cases, including murder, attempted murder and drug smuggling.He had also said Singh's detention followed international coordination and follow-up by Punjab Police agencies, while legal and diplomatic procedures were being pursued for his extradition or deportation to India.The latest extradition brings Singh back to India to face the criminal cases registered against him in Punjab.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Left with nothing, people in Gaza are forced to rent generators by the hour
articles.summary: Israel’s destruction of homes and infrastructure in Gaza has forced Palestinians to rent generators by the hour.
articles.body:
Families in Gaza City are forced to rent generators to pump water to their homes due to the lack of municipal electricity and water supplies functioning.

A shortage of spare parts and rising costs make it difficult for generator owners like Khalil Abu Ouda to provide essential services to their communities in Gaza.

Displaced families in Gaza are now paying for basic household chores like laundry, as the infrastructure that once allowed them to carry out these tasks at home has been severely disrupted.

Gaza City, Gaza Strip – For more than four hours, Hajj Rabhi al-Fairi, 79, has been standing outside his home in Gaza City with his children and neighbours waiting their turn to use a small generator.

The generator's owner pours in the fuel, starts a timer and switches on the machine.

Each family gets a few minutes to operate a pump that pushes water up to a storage tank on the roof, before the generator moves on to the next house.

For al-Fairi and his neighbours, this is how they get water.

"We have an old water pump, but there is no electricity to run it. We have to rent a generator," al-Fairi tells Al Jazeera.

Since the family returned to their home in October 2025, after fleeing a month earlier during Israel's assault on their neighbourhood, the generator has become a familiar sight on the streets of Nassr.

When it arrives, residents gather around it, each carrying a jerrycan of diesel to operate the machine, which they have to pay for themselves.

"We came back and found the place a tragedy," he says.

Their neighbourhood and home were badly damaged from years of Israeli bombing, with no municipal electricity or water supplies functioning. The family depends on an old pump – but without electricity, it cannot bring water up to the rooftop tank.

Each family needs only about seven or eight minutes to fill up their tanks, but with the number of flats in their building, the generator needs to be rented for about an hour.

The cost has also risen. Al-Rabhi says families used to pay about 80 to 90 shekels ($26-30) to rent a generator for an hour. At different times, the price has risen to about 100 or 120 shekels ($33-40) an hour, excluding the cost of diesel.

Khalil Abu Ouda, 39, takes a machine mounted on a horse-driven cart from one house to another. The generator's metal body is covered in black soot and grease, and white smoke rises from the engine when it operates.

At each house, Abu Ouda connects long electrical cables to the water pump. The cables stretch across the street as neighbours gather around the machine to wait their turn.

For Abu Ouda, this machine is both a service for the neighbourhood and an essential source of income for his family.

He says there are very few small, mobile generators, like his, left in working condition in Gaza. Many have broken down, while spare parts are difficult to find or too expensive to source due to Israel's siege.

Mechanics are also expensive to hire, while fuel and engine oil are increasingly scarce and costly.

"If I could, I would lower the price as much as possible," he says.

At the same time, demand has never been higher.

"People are under pressure and they need water. If I stayed working until morning, I would keep working," Abu Ouda says.

To cope with the demand, he often works for 10 to 12 hours a day, putting pressure on himself and the machine.

"But this is our livelihood. There is no alternative," he said.

With most Palestinians in Gaza having no home or losing their possessions due to Israel's genocidal war on Gaza, they have to rent or hire items or services for the most basic household chores.

This includes washing clothes, something once done at home but now impossible to do with no power.

Earlier in the war, Abeer Ghorab, 52, used to wash everything herself. Now she gathers clothes from her tent and takes them to a nearby laundry, where they can be washed and dried in far less time and with less effort.

"When these laundries started opening, they gave us some relief," Ghorab said.

The difference is particularly important in winter, when heavy clothes, blankets and bedding can take time to dry.

"In winter, the tracksuits are heavy. They need another day to dry," she said. "When I bring them here, they wash and dry them for me, and I get them back clean and dry. That really helps."

But due to a limited income, Ghorab cannot afford to use this laundry service every day.

Before the war, Ghorab had a washing machine, a refrigerator and regular electricity at home.

"Things we once took for granted have become dreams. Now we have to pay for every little thing we used to do at home."

Across Gaza, the infrastructure that once allowed families to carry out everyday tasks at home has been severely disrupted.

A recent United Nations assessment found that 91 percent of surveyed households experienced moderate-to-high water shortages in early August.

A separate damage assessment by the authority found that 107,941 of the 178,632 housing units inspected – about 60 percent – were severely damaged, destroyed or otherwise considered uninhabitable.

Water systems, electricity, sanitation and household appliances, which families relied on to manage daily life, have also been disrupted.

For families living in damaged homes, tents or makeshift shelters, everyday tasks must be paid for.

Fadi Abu Shawarb, 23, has worked at his family's al-Hurriya laundry for six years.

Before the war, the business relied on large, 50kg (110lb) washing machines for carpets, blankets and other heavy loads. But due to the high cost of operation, these machines are far too expensive to run.

"We started replacing the 50kg machines with 25kg ones because there is not enough electricity," Fadi says. "There are no solar panels, no reliable power, and the generators are always breaking down."

Most of his customers are displaced families who lack electricity, water or washing machines at home.

The laundry now handles about 20 to 30 loads a day, with clothes-washing among the most in-demand services.

A load costs six shekels ($2) when the laundry can use solar power and 12 shekels ($4) when it relies on a generator.

But even that is hard for people to pay. "People's situation is difficult," he says.

For Ghorab, the laundry is only one of the many expenses she now has to budget for.

"I feel like I'm going through a difficult time," she says. "I have to pay for every little thing in my day, and with how difficult things are, it's hard to keep up with everything."

articles.title: PM Modi, Brics leaders take part in joint tree plantation at Bharat Mandapam: Watch
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and leaders of Brics member countries on Saturday participated in a joint tree plantation at the lawns outside.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and leaders of Brics member countries on Saturday participated in a joint tree plantation at the lawns outside Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, where the 18th Brics Summit is being held.The leaders also posed together for a family photograph as part of the summit proceedings.This came as the Brics grouping on Saturday adopted a joint declaration by consensus, overcoming sharp differences between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia conflict following a series of back-channel negotiations.PM Modi announced the adoption of the declaration at the end of the opening day’s deliberations of the two-day India-hosted summit.The New Delhi Declaration, stated that the grouping would strengthen cooperation while respecting the national priorities, laws and regulations of individual member states.“We reaffirm our commitment to deepen cooperation in the field of competition law and policy among BRICS nations to foster fair, competitive, and resilient market environments across sectors, including critical and emerging areas, while respecting each State’s national priorities, laws and regulations,” the declaration said.The declaration noted discussions held under the theme, “Strengthening Cooperation to Promote Fair Competition, including in Renewable Energy Markets”, aimed at supporting sustainable energy transitions.It also encouraged continued cooperation among Brics competition authorities to identify and effectively address emerging competition challenges.The declaration expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for maximum restraint and avoidance of actions that could further aggravate the situation.Negotiations over the text went down to the wire, with Iran and the UAE initially taking firm positions. As Brics is a consensus-based grouping, any one member can block the adoption of a final joint declaration.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump says he would ‘love’ to see a united Ireland during visit for golf tournament
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said Saturday he would “love” ⁠to see Ireland unify with the U.K.’s Northern Ireland, remarks that received immediate pushback from unionists in the region.
articles.body: President Donald Trump said Saturday he would “love” ⁠to see Ireland unify with the U.K.’s Northern Ireland, remarks that received immediate pushback from unionists in the region. The comments come two weeks after new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said a referendum on Northern Ireland leaving the United Kingdom was “off the table.” Trump, who is visiting Dublin ahead of a golf tournament at one of his resorts, told reporters: “Well, I don’t want to ⁠cause any problems, but I will tell you, I’d ​love ⁠to see it unified. It’s going to happen eventually.” “Now the U.K. will have something to say about it ... but ​I think ⁠it would be a great thing,” ‌he added, while sitting next to Ireland’s Prime Minister Micheál Martin. At a later event with business leaders, Trump said that there was “no good answer” to the question, but reaffirmed: “It would be, I think, a very cool thing, to be honest with you.” Under the terms of the 1998 Good Friday Agreement, the power to call a referendum in Northern Ireland sits with the British government, with a duty to call a border poll if it appears likely that a majority of people in Northern Ireland would vote for Irish unification. The accord ended decades of violence between Irish nationalists seeking a united Ireland ‌and unionists who wanted Northern Ireland to remain part of the U.K. Polling continues to show a comfortable majority in Northern Ireland favor remaining in the U.K., though the gap has narrowed slightly since Britain’s departure from the European Union. Ireland remains in the bloc, with bespoke arrangements for Northern Ireland put in place to avert fears of a hard border and substantial trade barriers on the island. Asked by NBC News whether Downing Street had a response to the president’s remarks, a spokesperson said British Prime Minister Andy Burnham intends to adhere to the Good Friday Agreement. Under the accord, the matter would be reviewed “when public opinion has changed to the point at which the call has to be considered,” Burnham said earlier this week. The leader of Northern Ireland’s Democratic Unionist Party, Gavin Robinson, pushed back at Trump’s comments, stressing that Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom “because that is the settled democratic will of its people.” “President Trump knows better than most that elections matter,” he wrote in a post on X. “Northern Ireland’s constitutional future will be decided by the people of Northern Ireland, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington.” Kemi Badenoch, leader of Britain’s opposition Conservative Party, said Trump was “shooting from the hip as usual” in his remarks, adding: “This sort of loose talk about the future of democratic countries is deeply unhelpful and creates unnecessary tension.” Trump’s remarks did not win him much approval from the largest nationalist party, Sinn Féin, which is left-wing and deeply opposed to many of the U.S. president’s other political views. Chris Hazzard, an MP for the party, wrote on X: “Broken clocks and all that…” On his visit, Trump also met Irish President Catherine Connolly, who was elected head of state last year. When Trump last visited Ireland as president in 2019, Connolly, an outspoken politician with far-left foreign policy views, protested outside Shannon Airport in western Ireland. Some supporters had ‌urged her to speak out against U.S. military actions around the world and ​defend Ireland’s neutrality. Anti-war and anti-Trump protests were planned in Dublin and in ‌western Ireland near the Trump International Golf Links ⁠in Doonbeg. One protester held a Palestine flag over a fence near the ⁠Irish president’s residence. Ireland is one of the European Union’s most pro-Palestinian countries and in July passed a law restricting trade ‌in goods with settlements in ​the Israeli-occupied West Bank. U.S. lawmakers and the U.S. ‌ambassador to Ireland criticized the law. Strong ties Martin, the Irish prime minister, has so far avoided political flaps with the U.S. “The relationship between Ireland and the United ⁠States is very important economically,” he told reporters ahead of the visit. “It’s very, very significant both ways.” U.S.-owned companies employ about 10% of workers in Ireland after successive governments prioritized their jobs and corporate tax revenue over decades, handing Ireland the healthiest public finances in Europe in recent years. Including ‌Trump, eight sitting U.S. presidents have visited Ireland, ⁠starting with John F. Kennedy in 1963. But this trip has some hallmarks of ⁠Trump’s typical weekends, which often revolve around golf outings at his company’s properties. The Trump Organization took control in 2014 of ‌the Doonbeg course, which is ​hosting the Irish Open golf tournament this weekend. Trump ‌is expected to help present the trophy ​on Sunday to the tournament champion.

articles.title: Sweden’s election could bring far right a place at the heart of government
articles.summary: Swedes will vote on Sunday in a tight election that has effectively become a referendum on whether the far-right Sweden Democrats should join the government and ​cement their journey from pariahs to trusted partners in a country once seen as one of Europe’s most liberal.
articles.body: Swedes will vote on Sunday in a tight election that has effectively become a referendum on whether the far-right Sweden Democrats should join the government and ​cement their journey from pariahs to trusted partners in a country once seen as one of Europe’s most liberal. The party, with roots in the neo-Nazi fringe, has around 19% of ‌the vote, according to the latest polls, and the ruling center-right minority coalition has vowed to bring them into its bloc to secure Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson a second term in office. “We have agreed to campaign on a platform of building a common, majority government and that I will lead that government,” Kristersson told Reuters on the campaign trail in late August. The election will show whether Swedish voters want to deepen a political shift that has already upended decades of consensus ​on immigration and national identity, and turned one of Europe’s most open societies into a testing ground for tougher policies on integration, citizenship and border controls. Kristersson has credited his cooperation in parliament with ​the Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Akesson, since 2022, for delivering growth, lower prices for energy and food, reducing gang crime and shootings and cutting asylum numbers to record ⁠lows. He has promised to deepen ties after the September 13 vote and give the party cabinet positions. Over the last four years, the government has abolished permanent residency for refugees, tightened welfare rules and ​boosted expulsions of those without a right to stay. Asylum numbers have dropped to a 40-year low and while Kristersson says the focus will now be on integration, the Sweden Democrats want to go further. “In Sweden it is Swedish ​culture, the Swedish language, Swedish laws, Swedish norms, Swedish morals and Swedish traditions that apply,” Mattias Karlsson, Sweden Democrat lawmaker and one of Akesson’s closest allies, told Reuters. “If you can’t accept that, you have to find somewhere else to live.” Despite a consensus over tight immigration policies, many Swedes still feel a deep unease about the far right and polls point to a knife-edge vote with the centre-left opposition, which is backing Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson for prime minister, ​holding a small but narrowing lead. “If the Sweden Democrats enter government, that would have an enormously negative impact on the liberal ideals of our country,” said Birgitta Ohlsson, European Affairs minister from 2010 to 2014, ​and now a Center Party lawmaker. “We’ve already seen the effects while they’ve been outside government, and it would be ten times worse.” New landscape The rise of the far right has reshaped Europe’s political landscape, with such parties already sharing ‌power in ⁠countries including Finland, Italy, Croatia and the Czech Republic, while posing growing challenges in France and Germany. Akesson’s Sweden Democrats have spent the last four years as Kristersson’s main parliamentary backers and some analysts say the election may be less a watershed than a recognition of Akesson’s success in shedding the party’s extremist baggage. The party apologised in 2025 for past neo-Nazi and antisemitic views. “The election is a referendum on the Sweden Democrats; whether we continue to go down a far-right path,” Jan Guillou, author and political commentator, told Reuters. Policies that a decade ago many Swedes would have viewed as a rejection of the country’s liberal values have gained acceptance across much ​of the political spectrum. The blocs have also converged ​in several areas of key concern to voters ⁠with both promising stronger welfare, continued support for Ukraine, rearmament and measures to ease a cost-of-living crisis that has hit many households hard. “I think you’ll see a continued normalization of the Sweden Democrats,” said Lars Tragardh, a historian and author who led work on a government cultural heritage list criticised at the time by ​some as too narrow and exclusionary. “It’s time to tone down the hysteria.” Further shift? Critics, however, fear the Sweden Democrats’ promises to end multiculturalism, restore traditional Swedish ​values and ban some forms ⁠of Muslim dress could deepen social divisions and shift the political centre of gravity even further right. “I’m afraid more people will be expelled. I’m worried about the press, free speech and the freedom to demonstrate,” said Kurdo Baksi, an author and anti-racism campaigner, speaking on the sidelines of a pro-immigration demonstration in Stockholm. In a Facebook campaign message, Andersson said voters’ choice was not whether she or the incumbent Kristersson would become prime minister, but ⁠whether the Sweden ​Democrats would shape policy on defence, schools, culture and finance. “That would be a very different Sweden,” she said. Even if she wins, ​Andersson faces a daunting task in building a stable coalition. The four opposition parties, the Social Democrats, Greens, Left Party and Centre Party, broadly agree on increasing welfare and public spending. But they differ on key policies, from a tax on billionaires to whether Sweden ​should build new nuclear reactors, and the Centre Party refuses to sit in the same government as the Left Party.

articles.title: Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: Dos and don'ts to follow while bringing Ganpati Bappa home
articles.summary: Ganesh Chaturthi isn’t just the start of a festival; for millions, it’s an emotional homecoming. You see families scrubbing their homes, decorating ev.
articles.body: Ganesh Chaturthi isn’t just the start of a festival; for millions, it’s an emotional homecoming. You see families scrubbing their homes, decorating every corner, and setting up that special spot for Lord Ganesha, waiting to fill it with flowers, chants, music, and prayers. But with all that excitement, there’s also a layer of tradition woven through every step, from picking the idol to how you welcome Bappa, where he sits, and how you say goodbye during visarjan.In 2026, Ganesh Chaturthi falls on Monday, September 14. If you’re all about the details, the Chaturthi tithi begins at 7:06 am on September 14 and wraps up by 7:44 am on September 15. The main puja usually happens during the Madhyahna period, but it shifts depending on your city. Mumbai’s ideal window is between 11:20 am and 1:48 pm, while Kolkata goes from 10:18 am to 12:46 pm. It sounds complicated, but in most homes, the rituals adapt to local customs and what feels right for the family.Let’s get straight into what really matters: the dos and don’ts. These aren’t just tradition for tradition’s sake. They’re practical, thoughtful ways to honor Ganpati Bappa and make sure the celebration runs smoothly, and frankly, doesn’t leave a mess for anyone else or the planet.First off: don’t just clean for show. The idea is to create a space that’s worthy of puja: fresh, sacred, and genuinely inviting. Before the idol comes home, make sure your puja platform is spotless, draped with a clean cloth, and decked out with flowers, rangoli, mango-leaf torans, and diyas. The real point? Be ready for Bappa, not scrambling after he’s arrived.Next, picking the right idol is a big deal. There’s no one-size-fits-all answer about Ganesha’s posture or trunk direction — all those little details often depend on where you’re from or your family’s traditions. But most people go for a seated idol at home. These days, one thing matters more than ever: what the idol’s made of. Steer clear of plaster-of-Paris and chemical paints. They might be cheap and shiny, but they mess up our rivers and lakes after visarjan. So, go for clay or something biodegradable, with natural paints if possible. It’s a small step, but it really makes a difference environmentally.When it comes to welcoming Bappa, focus on devotion. Sure, some families create a spectacle with music, chants, and flower showers as they carry the idol inside, saying, “Ganpati Bappa Morya!” But the size of your celebration doesn’t matter as much as the feeling behind it. Handle the idol gently, place it with care on your prepared platform, and offer what tradition calls for: durva grass, flowers, fruits, modaks or laddoos.You can’t talk about Ganesh Chaturthi without mentioning family traditions. Rituals differ everywhere, from the number of days you keep the idol to the timing of visarjan. Some families celebrate for a day and a half, some three, five, seven, or the full ten days, ending on Anant Chaturdashi (September 25, 2026). The point is, there’s no “right” way. Don’t judge or stress over someone else’s customs, or feel pressured to follow another family’s script.Now, about decorations. It’s easy to get carried away with plastic, thermocol, and glitter, but that stuff just piles up after the festival and isn’t going anywhere. Instead, try cloth, paper, flowers, leaves, reusable items — anything that brings color and joy without lasting harm. Even your puja offerings can be composted, not dumped in rivers or lakes.Visarjan is always an emotional moment, saying goodbye to Bappa, hoping he takes your troubles with him. But remember, the environmental impact is real. If your city has artificial tanks or collection points, use them. Don’t take your idol to a lake or river on impulse; check what’s allowed. Home immersion is a nice option if you’ve got a clay idol and the space for it.One thing people sometimes forget: Ganesh Chaturthi isn’t a contest for the biggest idol or flashiest decorations. Don’t put safety at risk for spectacle. Keep wires away from water, place the idol securely, leave space so people aren’t scrambling. And be considerate with sound: fireworks, loudspeakers, music. Follow local rules and think about your neighbors.At its heart, bringing Ganpati home is about opening space in your life for prayer, reflection, and family. The rituals might vary from place to place and home to home, but the central idea is welcoming Ganesha, the remover of obstacles and symbol of wisdom, into your life.So, this Ganesh Chaturthi (September 14, 2026), do it with heart and mindfulness. Choose a clay idol, decorate simply, honor your own family’s traditions, and plan visarjan with care. Welcoming Bappa should bring blessings and joy, not leave behind harm to the world we live in. That’s what makes the festival, in every sense, truly special.Also Read: Happy Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: 50 heartfelt wishes, messages and quotes to share with family and friends and welcome Bappa with loveLooking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: 'Zero tolerance' on terror: Brics declaration strongly condemns Pahalgam attack
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Brics countries have strongly condemned the Pahalgam terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir that killed 26 people, reaffirming their com.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Brics countries have strongly condemned the Pahalgam terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir that killed 26 people, reaffirming their commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and calling for “zero tolerance” towards the menace.The condemnation was included in the New Delhi Declaration 2026, adopted at the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi on Saturday.The declaration also opposed double standards in countering terrorism and called for concerted action against all UN-designated terrorists and terrorist entities.“We express strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, whenever, wherever and by whomsoever committed,” the declaration said.It specifically condemned “in the strongest terms” the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on April 22, 2025, during which 26 people were killed and several others injured.Brics reaffirms stand against cross-border terrorThe Brics declaration reaffirmed the grouping’s commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens.The grouping said terrorism should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilisation or ethnic group. It also stressed that those involved in terrorist activities and their support must be held accountable and brought to justice in accordance with relevant national and international law.The declaration called for “zero tolerance for terrorism” and rejected double standards in countering terrorism.It also emphasised the primary responsibility of states in combating terrorism, while stressing that global efforts to prevent and counter terrorist threats must comply with international law, including the UN Charter and relevant international conventions and protocols.Brics welcomed the activities of its Counter-Terrorism Working Group and its five subgroups, which operate on the basis of the Brics Counter-Terrorism Strategy, Counter-Terrorism Action Plan and the Counter-Terrorism Working Group Position Paper.The grouping also called for the expeditious finalisation and adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism under the UN framework.The declaration further stressed the importance of countering extremism and radicalisation, particularly among younger generations, and called for greater cooperation among Brics countries and their competent authorities, including through the sharing of best practices.Pahalgam attack and India’s responseOn April 22, last year, 26 civilians were killed in a terrorist attack in the Baisaran meadow area near Pahalgam in South Kashmir, a major tourist destination.The victims were segregated by the attackers based on religion before being shot in front of their families, triggering widespread outrage.Security forces launched search operations in the surrounding areas following the attack, while investigations were expanded to trace the terrorist network and its logistical support.India responded with “Operation Sindoor” on May 7, 2025, carrying out precision strikes on terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.The operation marked a major escalation with Pakistan, followed by a four-day conflict that ended with a ceasefire on May 10, after Islamabad’s request.In the aftermath, Indian armed forces launched “Operation Mahadev” and tracked down and eliminated the three attackers involved in the Pahalgam killings.Declaration backs India, Brazil for greater UN roleBeyond terrorism, the New Delhi Declaration reaffirmed Brics' support for comprehensive reform of the United Nations, including the UN Security Council, with greater representation for developing countries.China and Russia, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, reiterated their support for the aspirations of India and Brazil to play a greater role in the UN, including its Security Council.The declaration called for greater and more meaningful participation and representation of emerging market and developing countries, as well as Least Developed Countries, in global decision-making processes.On Security Council reform, Brics said the process should make the body more democratic, representative, effective and efficient while increasing the representation of developing countries.“We stress that the UN Security Council reform is to lead to the amplified voice of the Global South,” the declaration said.The grouping also called for equitable geographical representation in the UN Secretariat and other international organisations, particularly at senior and decision-making levels.Brics raises concerns over trade measuresThe declaration also expressed serious concern over unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, saying they distort trade, threaten global supply chains and create uncertainty for international economic activity.Brics reaffirmed its support for reform of the World Trade Organization and called for an open, equitable, transparent, fair, inclusive, predictable and rules-based multilateral trading system, with the WTO at its core.The grouping also advocated the immediate restoration of an accessible, effective and fully functioning two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism and called for the appointment of new Appellate Body members without further delay.On unilateral coercive measures, Brics condemned sanctions that it said were contrary to international law and reiterated its opposition to unilateral coercive measures, including those not authorised by the UN Security Council.The New Delhi Declaration was adopted during the 18th Brics Summit, being hosted by India on September 12-13 under its 2026 chairship. India’s Brics chairship is guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: PMAY-U 2.0 nears 20 lakh homes as Centre approves 29,000 more houses
articles.summary: News News: The Centre government has approved more than 29,000 additional houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0), taking the total number.
articles.body: The Centre government has approved more than 29,000 additional houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0), taking the total number of sanctioned homes under the urban housing scheme to 18.77 lakh. The latest approvals come as the government steps up efforts to expand affordable housing supply and accelerate project implementation across urban areas.The approvals were cleared at the ninth meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), held on September 10, and cover Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Telangana, Tripura and Uttar Pradesh. The newly approved houses fall under the Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC) and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals.Affordable housing pipeline gets another pushThe latest sanctions take PMAY-U 2.0 closer to the 20-lakh-home milestone, reflecting the growing scale of the government's urban affordable housing programme.The scheme is targeted at economically weaker sections (EWS), low-income groups (LIG) and middle-income groups (MIG) with annual household income of up to Rs 9 lakh. Rather than following a single housing model, PMAY-U 2.0 provides assistance through beneficiary-led construction, affordable housing projects, rental housing and interest subsidy on eligible home loans.This allows households with different income levels and housing requirements to access support for construction, purchase or rental accommodation.Centre plans faster approvals for housing projectsThe government is also seeking to speed up the flow of projects from approval to sanction. Urban Development Secretary Satendra Singh said CSMC meetings will now be convened every second week of the month to ensure regular monitoring and accelerate implementation of PMAY-U 2.0.States and Union territories have been asked to submit duly approved projects by the end of each month so that they can be considered at the subsequent CSMC meeting.The move is aimed at creating a more regular project-sanctioning cycle and addressing bottlenecks that could delay the rollout of affordable housing projects.Women dominate PMAY-U 2.0 home ownershipWomen’s ownership remains one of the strongest features of the programme. Of the 18.77 lakh houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0, 17.19 lakh, or 92 percent, have been allotted to women.The houses are either in the name of the woman of the household or held jointly, giving women a direct stake in residential property ownership.The scheme has also targeted vulnerable sections, with 1.80 lakh houses allotted to senior citizens, while 3.25 lakh houses have been sanctioned for SC beneficiaries, 1.02 lakh for ST beneficiaries and 8.22 lakh for OBC beneficiaries.PMAY housing footprint crosses 1.25 crorePMAY-U 2.0 builds on the earlier PMAY-Urban programme. Together, the two schemes have resulted in more than 1.25 crore houses being sanctioned, with over 1 crore houses completed and delivered to beneficiaries.The latest approvals therefore represent not just an expansion of the affordable housing pipeline but another step towards increasing formal home ownership among lower- and middle-income urban households.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: At BRICS summit, China, Russia and India urge ‘maximum restraint’ in Middle East
articles.summary: The BRICS group of nations unanimously adopted a joint declaration on Saturday, expressing “deep concern” over the war ⁠in the Middle East and urging maximum restraint, advocating for a “multilateral approach” that respects national viewpoints.
articles.body: The BRICS group of nations unanimously adopted a joint declaration on Saturday, expressing “deep concern” over the war ⁠in the Middle East and urging maximum restraint, advocating for a “multilateral approach” that respects national viewpoints. The declaration, adopted on the first day of the BRICS leaders’ annual ⁠summit in New ​Delhi, ⁠comes at a time when the U.S. and Iran have resumed tit-for-tat strikes against each ⁠other, after a pause in fighting for much ​of ⁠August. The BRICS bloc includes ‌both Iran and the Washington-aligned United Arab Emirates, which was expected to make clinching a joint statement ‌consensus a particularly challenging task ‌for host India. “We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in the Middle East...call for exercising maximum restraint...avoiding ⁠actions that could further aggravate the situation,” the ‘New Delhi Declaration’ said. The declaration also reiterated the commitment of member nations to a peaceful resolution of international disputes “through dialogue, consultation, and diplomacy”. In addition, they voiced concerns about the rise of “unilateral tariff ‌and non-tariff measures” that distort trade, against the ​backdrop of U.S. sanctions against ‌Tehran amid its war with ⁠the country, and against Russia over its ⁠conflict with Ukraine. China urges peacemaker role Chinese President Xi Jinping urged the BRICS bloc to be a peacemaker in the ⁠Middle East conflict, in an address to a summit of member countries in New Delhi on Saturday. China will work with other ⁠BRICS members in ​that ⁠role, as the war “does not serve the common interests of the international ⁠community,” state-run CCTV quoted Xi as ​saying. BRICS ⁠groups Brazil, Russia, ‌India, China and South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab ‌Emirates. It was set up ‌in 2009 to challenge a world order dominated by the United States and its ⁠Western allies. Together, its members account for more than 40% of the world’s population and almost a quarter of the global economy. The Chinese leader called the bloc a “leading group” in the Global South ‌and a model of self-reliance ​among emerging and developing countries ‌that should promote ⁠innovation-driven development. China-India ties The visit for the summit is Xi’s first to India in seven years and comes as the Asian ⁠neighbours cautiously rebuild ties ​that ⁠were badly damaged after a military clash on their disputed Himalayan border in 2020 ⁠in which 20 Indian and four Chinese ​soldiers ⁠were killed. The Xi-Modi meeting, scheduled ‌for Saturday evening, will be their third in three years, a spokesperson for China’s foreign ministry said on Friday. China “is ⁠willing” to work together with India, to view two-way relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, properly manage differences, and be “good neighbours and friends, as well as mutually supportive partners,” the spokesperson said.
