articles.title: Trump says a unified Ireland is ‘going to happen eventually’
articles.summary: President Trump on Saturday expressed optimism about the reunification of Ireland during a meeting with Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin in Dublin. The president, who is visiting his Irish golf course this weekend for a major golf tournament, said he would “love” to see the joining of the Republic of Ireland and the U.K.’s Northern Ireland. …
articles.body:
President Trump on Saturday expressed optimism about the reunification of Ireland during a meeting with Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin in Dublin.

The president, who is visiting his Irish golf course this weekend for a major golf tournament, said he would “love” to see the joining of the Republic of Ireland and the U.K.’s Northern Ireland.

“I’d love to see it unified,” Trump said. “I think that’d be a great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. It’s going to happen eventually.”

He pointed to Martin, adding, “You’ve got the right man over here to get it moving.”

The president noted that “the U.K. will have something to say about it, obviously.”

Previous U.S. presidents have typically avoided directly commenting on this contentious issue. Ireland’s split followed decades of violent conflict, called “the Troubles,” in Northern Ireland over whether to unite with the rest of Ireland or to remain part of the U.K.

The Good Friday Agreement, which the U.S. helped broker to end this conflict, gives the secretary of Northern Ireland the ability to call a border poll if it seems likely that a majority of people in the region would support Irish unification.

On Wednesday, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham told British parliament members that he was “not aware that there is majority support for another referendum.”

“Until that changes, there will not be one,” he added.

Kemi Badenoch, the leader of the U.K.’s Conservative Party, slammed Trump’s comments in a social media post on Saturday.

“President Trump is shooting from the hip as usual, just like he did with Greenland and Canada becoming the 51st state,” she wrote. “This sort of loose talk about the future of democratic countries is deeply unhelpful and creates unnecessary tension.

“Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom,” Badenoch continued. “At a time when separatists are in power in Scotland, Wales and NI, we need a Government that will defend the Union clearly and confidently.”

Gavin Robinson, the leader of the U.K.’s Democratic Unionist Party who represents Northern Ireland in Parliament, also reacted to the president’s comment in a social media post .

“President Trump knows better than most that elections matter,” Robinson said. “Northern Ireland’s constitutional future will be decided by the people of Northern Ireland, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington.”

Robinson expressed his confidence that the people of Northern Ireland “will continue to choose the UK and the security it offers.”

articles.title: Train derails in France and injures 44 as authorities investigate possible sabotage
articles.summary: French authorities are investigating whether sabotage caused a train derailment that injured 44 people in Normandy, after a piece of rail was found on the track.
articles.body: French authorities are investigating whether sabotage caused a train derailment that injured 44 people in Normandy, after a piece of rail was found on the track, police told The Associated Press on Saturday. The regional train was carrying 186 passengers from Rouen to Caen when it derailed Friday evening at Cléon, in the Seine-Maritime department of northwestern France. An 18-year-old woman was among the injured and was evacuated by helicopter to Rouen University Hospital, police said. A spokeswoman for the French national police communications service, known as SICOP, said that the piece of rail found on the track was “probably” linked to the derailment. She spoke on condition of anonymity because she wasn’t authorized to be publicly named in line with police policy. Investigators were working to establish whether the circumstances were accidental or involved sabotage, the service said. The prosecutor’s office remained cautious about drawing conclusions, according to the police. France’s previous rail disasters include the July 2013 derailment at Brétigny-sur-Orge, south of Paris, which killed seven people. In November 2015, a high-speed TGV train carrying out tests derailed at Eckwersheim, near Strasbourg, killing 11. More recently, a crash involving two high-speed trains at Adamuz in southern Spain killed 46 people and injured more than 100 in January, according to the Andalusian regional government.

articles.title: Donald Trump's childhood home was bought for $835,000 in 2025; after a $500,000 renovation, it has sold for $1.93 million
articles.summary: News News: A house in Queens where US President Donald Trump spent the earliest years of his childhood has found a new owner, selling for $1.93 million after und.
articles.body: A house in Queens where US President Donald Trump spent the earliest years of his childhood has found a new owner, selling for $1.93 million after undergoing a dramatic renovation.The Tudor-style property in New York City's Jamaica Estates had been vacant for years and was reportedly in poor condition when developer Tommy Lin purchased it for $835,000 in 2025. Eight months and about $500,000 in renovation work later, the five-bedroom house has nearly doubled in value.The sale closed at $1.93 million, just $70,000 below its latest asking price, according to the New York Post. The property had initially been listed for $2.3 million before its price was reduced.But the home's biggest selling point was not simply its size or its renovation. It was the name attached to its history.The house where Trump spent his early childhoodLocated at 85-15 Wareham Place in Jamaica Estates, the approximately 3,100-square-foot house was built by Trump's father, real estate developer Fred Trump.Donald Trump lived in the property with his family during the earliest years of his life, until he was about four years old. The family later moved to a much larger house nearby, where Trump spent much of his childhood.The Wareham Place property is considerably more modest than the lavish residences associated with Trump today. That contrast has helped make the house an unusual piece of his personal and real estate history. Before Trump became a businessman and later a US president, the property was simply the home of a young boy growing up in Queens. Its presidential connection has since turned the house into a piece of real estate with a story attached to it.From $835,000 fixer-upper to $1.93 million saleWhen Lin bought the property in 2025, it was far from its current condition. The house had reportedly been vacant for years and had suffered damage from a burst pipe. Mold had also become a problem, while feral cats had taken over parts of the property.Lin then embarked on an eight-month renovation costing approximately $500,000. The work transformed the interiors while retaining the home's Tudor-style exterior. The renovated property now features a chef's kitchen, herringbone flooring and spa-like bathrooms.The five-bedroom, four-bathroom house covers about 3,100 square feet, giving the buyer both modern interiors and a connection to a particularly unusual chapter of American political and real estate history.The property's history has also made it something of a celebrity real estate curiosity. It has changed hands several times over the years, with an earlier sale in 2017 reportedly fetching $2.14 million. At one point, the home was also offered as an Airbnb rental.A house whose value goes beyond its wallsThe latest sale illustrates how a property's historical association can become a major part of its market appeal.For an ordinary five-bedroom home, a lengthy vacancy, water damage and mold would likely be significant drawbacks. In this case, however, the property's connection to Trump added another layer of interest for potential buyers. The house's location also matters. Jamaica Estates is an affluent Queens neighborhood that has long been associated with Trump's early life. The family moved within the same neighborhood when Donald was young, and his father built several properties there.The Wareham Place home has previously attracted attention precisely because of its unusual combination of modest suburban architecture and presidential history. It was put on the market during Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, initially for $1.65 million. The property was later sold at auction, and attempts were made to sell it again in subsequent years.Now, after years of changing ownership and a major renovation, the property has once again changed hands. The $1.93 million sale means the house has come a long way from the neglected property Lin purchased for $835,000.And for its new owner, that history now comes with freshly renovated floors, a modern kitchen, spa-style bathrooms and a nearly $2 million price tag.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: First Akash, then Ishan, now Deepika: A new twist in Mayawati's succession story takes another turn
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati on Saturday ruled out any political position for her brother Anand Kumar's sons, Akash Anand and Ishan A.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati on Saturday ruled out any political position for her brother Anand Kumar's sons, Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, calling it her “final decision”, while allowing for the possibility of her niece Kumari Deepika Anand assisting her father with party responsibilities.The announcement came days after Mayawati “freed” her nephew Akash Anand from the party, adding a fresh turn to the BSP's leadership and succession debate ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.In a lengthy post on X in Hindi, Mayawati said she remained focused on the interests of the “Bahujan Samaj family” and reiterated her opposition to political nepotism.“Like Kanshi Ram ji, I too have always kept my brothers, sisters, young family members, and close relations away from positions as MP, MLA, minister, or any other post offering political benefit, by confining them to party work,” she said.Mayawati said Anand Kumar had remained with her and had been handling important party responsibilities under her supervision.“Not only this, since I am unmarried, I am forced to keep one of my siblings -- finally my youngest brother Anand Kumar -- with me. He not only takes care of me but has also been carrying out important party responsibilities under my supervision for a long time. However, if his family members also take advantage of this, then it will not be in the interest of the party and the movement,” she said.Making her decision explicit, Mayawati said, “Therefore, today it is my final decision and pledge that in return, none of his sons, in particular, will be allowed to engage in politics by holding any position, big or small, within the BSP.”She said Anand Kumar could instead seek assistance from his daughter, who is currently studying law.“If Anand Kumar, while remaining with me, needs another member to assist him, then in the current political situation, he can seek the help of his only daughter, Kumari Deepika Anand,” Mayawati said.She added that if Deepika Anand was unwilling, her father could, with the party's consensus, hand over his responsibilities to another “missionary worker” from the party's Dalit community.“This is the need of the hour and in the party's best interest,” she said.Mayawati also invoked Kanshi Ram's opposition to nepotism, saying she remained committed to the principle as his disciple.Meanwhile, she announced a parallel push for younger leadership, saying the BSP was working to ensure around 50 per cent participation of Gen-Z in its organisation. She said the party was also prioritising “dedicated and young talents from all sections of society” as candidates for the Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab Assembly elections due in 2027.The BSP chief said the aim was “so that the constitutional values can rapidly flourish in the country through the new generation”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Differences should not become disputes': PM Modi says India-China ties should be guided by 3 mutuals
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese president Xi Jinping on Saturday reaffirmed the need to take a “strategic and long term perspectiv.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese president Xi Jinping on Saturday reaffirmed the need to take a “strategic and long term perspective” of India-China ties, while stressing border peace, adherence to existing agreements and a “fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable” resolution of the boundary question, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said.The two leaders met in New Delhi on the sidelines of the Brics Summit and “welcomed the steady progress in India-China bilateral relations” since their last meeting in Tianjin in August 2025.“Differences should not become disputes,” PM Modi said, stressing that both sides must be guided by three principles — “mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest”.Also read: Reset in India-China ties? PM Modi offers 'opportunity' to Xi during bilateral talksAccording to the MEA, PM Modi emphasised that “peace and tranquility in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations”. He also underlined the need for both countries to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.The two leaders “expressed commitment” to a “fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question”, with the process to proceed from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relationship and the long-term interests of the two peoples, the MEA said.The meeting also covered efforts to expand people-to-people ties. Both sides “underscored the need to further promote cultural exchanges, business linkages and greater mobility” between India and China.On economic and trade relations, the leaders agreed on the need to address each other’s concerns, including the “structural trade imbalance and supply chain issues”, while facilitating “meaningful and predictable market access”.The discussions also extended to regional and global issues, with the two leaders agreeing that India and China should “continue to expand common ground” in addressing shared challenges.The MEA said PM Modi appreciated China’s support for India’s Brics chairship and its contribution to the success of the Brics Summit 2026.The meeting comes as New Delhi and Beijing work to consolidate the progress made in bilateral ties since the military standoff along the Line of Actual Control.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bus driver threatened with knife as bus hijacked in Omagh and chased in police pursuit to Strabane
articles.summary: Passengers were allowed to leave the bus but the driver was kept on board during the hijacking.
articles.body:
A man has been arrested after a hijacked bus was brought to a stop after a police chase.

The driver of the bus was threatened at knife point by a man, who then allowed passengers to leave the bus. However, the bus driver was kept on board.

Videos circulating on social media appear to show a Translink Goldliner coach being driven at speed through residential streets while being chased by a Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) patrol car.

Police said the bus was hijacked in the Beltany Road area of Omagh, Co Tyrone, shortly before 13:00 BST on Saturday.

The man who hijacked the bus then made off in the direction of Newtownstewart and a pursuit ensued along the A5 through Victoria Bridge and Sion Mills. The pursuit lasted nearly 20 miles.

"The bus was eventually stopped in the Head of the Town area of Strabane and a man, aged in his 30s was removed from the bus and subsequently arrested," said a PSNI spokesperson.

The police said one man has been taken to hospital for treatment for his injuries.

A number of reports of collisions involving the stolen bus and other vehicles, including a police car and damage to property have been received by police, who are appealing for information.

The Fountain Street and Drumallagh areas in Strabane remain closed at this time and the public are asked to avoid the area.

Sinn Féin councillor Brian Barney Harte said a wall was damaged at the side of a house in Strabane during the pursuit.

He said people were shocked and distressed, adding that his thoughts were with those involved.

"How there has not been a fatality is only by a miracle," he said.

"Numerous cars and properties have been damaged and people have told me of near misses of pedestrians, some pushing prams."

Barney said the bus came to a stop right beside a children's play park and that a police helicopter was involved in the chase.

A spokesperson for public transport operator Translink NI said: "We can confirm an incident occurred involving a Goldliner coach travelling on the Beltany Road in Omagh this afternoon.

"We are assisting the PSNI with their investigation including use of onboard CCTV and would ask anyone with information relating to the incident to contact the police."

articles.title: Yemen war escalates: Nearly 50,000 flee homes as Iran-backed Houthi offensive threatens Red Sea trade
articles.summary: Middle East News: More than 46,000 people have been forced to flee their homes in Yemen in the past week as a rapid Houthi offensive along the Red Sea coast threatens t.
articles.body: More than 46,000 people have been forced to flee their homes in Yemen in the past week as a rapid Houthi offensive along the Red Sea coast threatens to push the country back into a wider war and deepen an already severe humanitarian crisis.According to The Guardian, entire villages have been emptied as Houthi forces, backed by Iran, seized a string of towns from forces aligned with the US- and Saudi-backed Yemeni government.The UN International Organization for Migration (IOM) said 46,000 people had been displaced across the Taiz and Hodeidah governorates, with many families being forced to flee for a second or third time.The latest fighting marks the most serious escalation in Yemen since a UN-brokered truce in 2022.The UN special envoy for Yemen, Hans Grundberg, warned that the country had entered “a new and more dangerous phase of war”, saying the renewed fighting could draw Yemen deeper into the wider regional conflict.Families flee with little more than clothesFor civilians caught in the fighting, the latest offensive has meant abandoning homes with little warning.For those who have escaped the latest fighting, the immediate concern is survival. “We managed to leave, but others remain trapped there,” one displaced man, Mohammed Khudairi, told the Guardian.The New York Times reported that some families fled after shells landed near their houses, while others were forced to make difficult journeys on foot or in improvised vehicles.One displaced Yemeni, Al-Megdad Hashem, said 34 people, including his family and elderly parents, crowded into a truck normally used to transport construction material after shelling wounded two people. “It was difficult to take anything,” he was quoted as saying by the NYT.The Guardian reported that aid workers were struggling to keep pace with the rapidly changing situation, with civilians in need of emergency shelter, food, drinking water, healthcare and other assistance. “The scale of displacement is increasing rapidly,” Joe Lowry, an IOM spokesperson, said.Houthi advance threatens key Red Sea routeThe Houthi offensive has also raised concerns beyond Yemen because of its proximity to the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a crucial maritime chokepoint linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.Houthi forces this week captured the strategic port city of Mokha and an island in the waterway, according to Yemeni officials cited by the New York Times. The moves give the Iran-backed group a foothold near the Bab al-Mandab, through which major energy and commercial shipments pass.Houthis' control of key areas near the strait could have serious consequences for global trade. Any attempt to close the chokepoint could force ships to take a much longer route around southern Africa, adding thousands of nautical miles to journeys.The fighting has already added to pressure on oil prices, with the Guardian reporting that crude had risen above USD 100 a barrel after trading closer to $80 for weeks.Yemen's humanitarian crisis worsensThe renewed fighting comes as Yemen was already facing one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. More than 18 million people are facing acute food insecurity, while 2.2 million children are acutely malnourished, according to figures cited by the New York Times.The crisis has been compounded by a shortage of humanitarian funding. The World Food Programme has suspended food aid in some areas and reduced monthly cash assistance, while Yemen's healthcare system remains under severe pressure.The NYT reported that more than 17,600 measles cases had been recorded in Yemen in the first seven months of the year. At a hospital in the government-held city of Marib, maternity and obstetric services have also been suspended to make room for trauma patients.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Newcastle Mercury Prize Fringe to showcase upcoming artists
articles.summary: A week of performances and workshops are organised ahead of the Mercury Prize's return to Newcastle.
articles.body:
Dozens of fringe events in the run-up to the Mercury Prize's second year in Newcastle will showcase upcoming musicians, organisers say.

The city will see live performances, listening parties, screenings, workshops and talks from 15 to 22 October, featuring artists from across north-east England.

A live edition of BBC Introducing will come from The Glasshouse International Centre for Music, headlined by Sunderland's Tom A. Smith.

Presenter Neave Farry, from Ferryhill, is curating and hosting a free acoustic event at the Grainger Market and said the "rest of England is waking up to the beautiful scene that we've got in the North East".

The prestigious music industry awards will return to Newcastle's Utilita Arena on 22 October, having never previously been held outside of London before 2025.

Sam Fender won the accolade and £25,000 prize last year in front of his home crowd .

Olivia Dean and Sir Paul McCartney's albums are among those nominated this year, in recognition of artistic achievement .

Grainger Market unplugged on 17 October will see acoustic sets from emerging artists throughout the day.

Farry said a recent refurbishment of the market to add a performance space "looks and sounds fantastic".

Polyvinyl are one of the bands performing and drummer Jamie Round said a "North East crowd is the best crowd you're going to get".

"You'll play the gig and everyone will be so supportive but then at the end you'll have people coming and talking to you, having a proper conversation," he said.

"It's different, you don't get that anywhere else."

Round said: "Not only is it a free event but it's also showcasing local art.

"And it's so valuable, especially right now when it's such a struggle for local arts to even be supported."

The fringe events are funded by Newcastle City Council and the BPI, which organises the Mercury Prize, and organised by Generator.

articles.title: Bulgaria says fire at ammunition plant might be an act of sabotage
articles.summary: The Bulgarian Interior Ministry has not ruled out sabotage as the cause of a fire at an ammunition depot in the central part of the country, it said on Satur...
articles.body:
Bulgarian Interior Ministry is investigating the possibility of sabotage as the cause of a fire at an ammunition depot belonging to defence contractor EMKO, which supplies ammunition to Ukraine.

This incident marks the second explosion in just over a month at an EMKO site, with no injuries reported at the Gorni Varpishta location in Bulgaria.

Safety measures at all ammunition depots in Bulgaria will now be inspected following a series of incidents at defence facilities in EU member states supporting Ukraine against Russia.

The Bulgarian Interior Ministry has not ruled out sabotage as the cause of a fire at an ammunition depot in the central part of the country, it said on Saturday.

This was the second explosion in just over a month at a site belonging to the Bulgarian defence contractor EMKO, which supplies ammunition to Ukraine.

No one was injured in the incident at the Gorni Varpishta site in the early hours of Saturday morning.

"We do not rule out external interference, but if storage conditions are not adhered to (...) one does not necessarily rule out the other," said Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev at the scene. He did not explicitly mention Russia.

The interior minister announced that safety measures at every ammunition depot in Bulgaria would now be inspected.

There has been a series of incidents at facilities belonging to defence companies in EU member states that are supporting Ukraine in the face of Russia's war against its neighbour.

On August 13, a fire led to an explosion at an ammunition factory not far from the Italian capital, Rome. The exact cause of the incident was not immediately known.

Also in August, a building belonging to the Estonian defence company Milrem Robotics in Tallinn is reported to have been severely damaged by a fire.

In Romania, which shares a border with Ukraine, the SRI intelligence service stated on September 8 that it had foiled a sabotage operation coordinated by Russia.

It is suspected that the explosions at EMKO sites in Bulgaria could form part of a wider pattern of suspected or confirmed acts of sabotage targeting Ukraine's military supply chains within NATO territory.

articles.title: Ted Cruz got booed so loudly during 'College GameDay' interview you couldn't hear a thing he said
articles.summary: Ted Cruz was booed so loudly during his "College GameDay" appearance in Austin that his pitch for the "Save College Sports Act" was nearly drowned out.
articles.body: Nothing says college football like Ted Cruz and Rece Davis. Or, you know, something like that. Cruz made a nearly 10-minute cameo on ESPN's College GameDay Saturday morning to push the "Protect College Sports Act," which is currently collecting dust in Congress. Among the many things Cruz said, the most notable was this: "I think we're going to get the (60) votes." PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT STALLS IN OVERNIGHT SENATE SHOWDOWN, VOTE PUSHED TO SEPTEMBER AFTER CHAOTIC EVENING Before we get into the nuts and bolts of the bill — and believe me, I'll keep that brief — we have to address the elephant in the room. Cruz, a Texas senator, got booed so loudly during the entirety of the interview — which took place on the Longhorns' Austin campus — that you could barely hear a word he said. Fair is fair, and I have to be fair here ... This was a tough watch: Ted Cruz's College GameDay hit didn't go great Goodness gracious. Just a brutal scene here for Ted Cruz. You couldn't hear a thing he said, for the most part, the entire interview. At one point, it sounded like it was finally dying down, only for the "Ted you suck" chants to take over. Now, I have no idea why they were booing Ted Cruz. The truth is, they don't, either. Do you think a bunch of hungover college kids who haven't slept since Thursday give a you-know-what about the "Protect College Sports Act"? Of course not! They couldn't tell you one single thing in the act, or what it's about, or whether it's good or not. They're not booing the bill itself — which, in theory, will help stabilize the current NIL landscape in college sports, which has spiraled out of control. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Nick Saban has backed it. Deion Sanders was on a commercial supporting the bill immediately following Cruz's appearance. PRESIDENT TRUMP PUSHES LAWMAKERS ON LEGISLATION AS 'PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT' HANGS ON BY A THREAD Still, it's struggling to pass. Shocking! That almost never happens in Congress. As for the booing ... I assume it's because Cruz A) is a Republican and college campuses lean left, B) students don't want politics on a sports show, C) Austin is a liberal town, or C) all the above. TED CRUZ URGES SENATE TO STAY IN WASHINGTON UNTIL PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT PASSES THIS WEEK He's clearly a Longhorns fan, so you would think that would've been his saving grace here. But not in Austin, which is a liberal haven in a deep red state. Credit to ESPN for having a Republican on its airwaves, though. That's a big step! Just wish we could've heard a thing he said.

articles.title: At least seven killed in fire at prison in northern Syria
articles.summary: Inmates rioted following protests in the city of Kobane over the killing of former Kurdish fighter, state media reports.
articles.body:
At least seven inmates have been killed and others injured after a fire broke out at a prison in a predominantly Kurdish town in northern Syria.

The fire started when inmates at a jail in Kobane rioted over tensions that had erupted in the town on Friday, Syrian state-run news agency SANA reported on Saturday. However, the cause of the blaze is yet to be officially confirmed.

“Dozens were injured, burned or suffocated following a riot,” state TV reported.

According to the UK-based Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, the riot began overnight after authorities decided to transfer some inmates to another facility in Aleppo.

On Friday, protests broke out in Kobane over the killing of a former Kurdish fighter, Sami Sheikhmous Hiso.

Hiso’s body was returned to Kobane on Thursday after he was kidnapped, according to the AFP news agency. AFP reported that his body showed wounds caused by gunfire.

The protests and prison riot highlight the divisions still present in Syria following the ousting of longtime leader Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.

Syria’s new head of state, President Ahmed al-Sharaa, has pledged to oversee an inclusive administration and govern for all. However, his pledge has been set back by bouts of sectarian violence involving government forces.

In January, Damascus and Syria’s Kurdish community reached an integration agreement, which has since seen Kurdish civilian and military institutions become part of the Syrian state . The prison in Kobane is still administered by Kurdish authorities and is yet to be handed over to the central government.

Demonstrations against Hiso’s death turned violent on Friday, leading to arrests, according to Kurdish news outlet Rudaw. Rudaw reported that some of the protesters attacked security forces and were being held in the prison at the time of the riot and fire.

Syrian presidential adviser Mazloum Abdi (also known as Mazloum Kobani) arrived in Kobane on Saturday and has been meeting with senior officials there, according to media reports.

Abdi was appointed presidential adviser last month, days after announcing the dissolution of the Syrian Democratic Forces, a Kurdish coalition of armed groups that he led.
